text:
Tomas Hertl is 33 and still the forward who makes Vegas look like the better team almost every shift. At five on five the Golden Knights have taken 63% of the expected goals with him on the ice (expected goals measure the quality of chances), about 12 points better than when he sits. That, more than the 18 points in 24 games, is his season.

The points are real too, seven of them on the power play, which fits his profile: Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming with the man advantage, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man, 8.2 primary shot assists per 60.

His goals arrive in clumps. All four in his last ten games came on two nights, Nov 3 in Pittsburgh and Nov 8 in Buffalo, and he hasn't scored in six since. Nothing about that looks like luck in either direction: nine goals on 10.2 expected is right where a shooter like him lives.

What to watch: Vegas has lost four straight, three of them after regulation, while Hertl's line keeps winning the shot battle. Someone on it needs to finish.
headline: Hertl tilts the ice, and the goals come in bunches
